# Introduction

## What this internship is about {.intro-bigger}

- **3-month internship** focused on text classification
- Central use case: **NAF** — classifying business activities from free text *(more on this later)*
- Explored a range of modeling approaches, from simple to more complex — comparing **what works, what doesn't, and why**
- Common thread: not just accuracy — being able to **explain** why a model chose a given label
- Today: a **selection of key results** — the full experimental report is on GitHub

# Concepts

## Models Used: FastText {.center}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="34%"}
- Words are embedded, then simply **averaged** (mean pooling)
- Word order and context between tokens are **ignored**
- Minimal parameters — very fast to train and to run
- The baseline behind the model **already in production** for NAF coding
:::

## Models Used: FastText + Transformer Encoder (FATE) {.center}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="34%"}
- Same embeddings, but first passed through **N transformer encoder layers** (self-attention + feed-forward)
- Words gain **context from their neighbors** before being pooled
- Everything downstream — pooling, linear head — is unchanged
- More expressive representation — but heavier and slower to train/run
:::

::::

## Aggregation Method: Mean Pooling {.center}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="34%"}
- Every token embedding contributes **equally** to the sentence vector: $v = \frac{1}{T}\sum_t e_t$
- No notion of importance — a keyword and a stopword count the same
- The **same pooled vector** $v$ is then reused by the linear head, for every class alike
- Simple and fast, a strong baseline — but blind to *which* words actually drove the decision
:::

::: {.column width="66%"}

::::

## Aggregation Method: Label Attention {.center}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="34%"}
- Each class $c$ learns its own **attention query**, giving weights $\alpha_{c,t}$ over the tokens (softmax, sums to 1)
- Class vector: $v_c = \sum_t \alpha_{c,t}\, e_t$ — a **different weighted combination per class**
- The weights double as an **explanation**: which words mattered, *for which class*
- More expressive than mean pooling — and interpretable **by construction**, not after the fact
:::

::: {.column width="66%"}

## Captum: Explaining a Prediction After the Fact {.center}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="34%"}
- **Captum (Integrated Gradients)**: a post-hoc method — explains any differentiable model, no architecture change needed
- Interpolates between a **baseline** (e.g. an empty input) and the actual input, accumulating gradients along the path
- Output: one **attribution score per token** — how much each word pushed the prediction toward the predicted class
:::

::: {.column width="66%"}
```{=html}
<div style="zoom:1;">
  <div style="border:2px solid #d0d0d0;border-radius:14px;background:#fff;
              padding:20px 26px;box-sizing:border-box;width:640px;
              display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:16px;
              box-shadow:0 2px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.06);">

    <div style="text-align:center;font-size:10.5px;color:#999;font-family:monospace;">
      IG(xₜ) = (xₜ − x′ₜ) · (1/m) Σₖ ∂Fc/∂xₜ (x′ + (k/m)(x−x′))
    </div>

    <!-- Step 1 -->
    <div class="ig-step">
      <div class="ig-badge">1</div>
      <div style="flex:1;">
        <div class="ig-title">Pick a baseline — a neutral reference input</div>
        <div style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:18px;">
          <div style="display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;">
            <div class="cg-baseline">∅</div>
            <div class="ig-sub">baseline x′ (zero embedding)</div>
          </div>
          <div style="font-size:16px;color:#ccc;">vs.</div>
          <div style="display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;">
            <div style="display:flex;gap:6px;">
              <div class="cg-tok">sells</div>
              <div class="cg-tok">organic</div>
              <div class="cg-tok">vegetables</div>
              <div class="cg-tok">online</div>
            </div>
            <div class="ig-sub">actual input x</div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Step 2 -->
    <div class="ig-step">
      <div class="ig-badge">2</div>
      <div style="flex:1;">
        <div class="ig-title">Walk the straight line from x′ to x in m steps, and measure the gradient at each point</div>
        <div style="display:flex;align-items:flex-end;gap:0;padding-top:6px;">
          <div class="ig-pt"><div class="ig-bar" style="height:5px;"></div><div class="ig-dot"></div><div class="ig-a">α=0</div></div>
          <div class="ig-pt"><div class="ig-bar" style="height:12px;"></div><div class="ig-dot"></div><div class="ig-a">.2</div></div>
          <div class="ig-pt"><div class="ig-bar" style="height:20px;"></div><div class="ig-dot"></div><div class="ig-a">.4</div></div>
          <div class="ig-pt"><div class="ig-bar" style="height:29px;"></div><div class="ig-dot"></div><div class="ig-a">.6</div></div>
          <div class="ig-pt"><div class="ig-bar" style="height:37px;"></div><div class="ig-dot"></div><div class="ig-a">.8</div></div>
          <div class="ig-pt"><div class="ig-bar" style="height:44px;"></div><div class="ig-dot"></div><div class="ig-a">α=1</div></div>
        </div>
        <div style="display:flex;justify-content:space-between;font-size:9.5px;color:#888;padding-top:2px;">
          <span>x′ + α(x−x′)</span><span>bar height = |∂Fc/∂x| at that point</span>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Step 3 -->
    <div class="ig-step">
      <div class="ig-badge">3</div>
      <div style="flex:1;">
        <div class="ig-title">Average the m gradients, then scale by how far each word is from its baseline</div>
        <div style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;">
          <div class="ig-op">1/m Σ</div>
          <div class="ig-arrow-h">──▶</div>
          <div class="ig-op">avg gradient</div>
          <div class="ig-arrow-h">──▶</div>
          <div class="ig-op">× (x − x′)</div>
          <div class="ig-arrow-h">──▶</div>
          <div class="ig-op" style="border-color:#c62828;background:#ffebee;color:#b71c1c;">IGₜ</div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Result -->
    <div class="ig-step">
      <div class="ig-badge" style="background:#c62828;">✓</div>
      <div style="flex:1;">
        <div class="ig-title">Result: one attribution score per token</div>
        <div style="display:flex;gap:8px;">
          <div class="cg-attr" style="background:rgba(211,47,47,.15);color:#4a0000;"><span>sells</span><small>0.04</small></div>
          <div class="cg-attr" style="background:rgba(211,47,47,.80);color:#fff;"><span>organic</span><small>0.51</small></div>
          <div class="cg-attr" style="background:rgba(211,47,47,.55);color:#fff;"><span>vegetables</span><small>0.38</small></div>
          <div class="cg-attr" style="background:rgba(211,47,47,.10);color:#4a0000;"><span>online</span><small>0.07</small></div>
        </div>
        <div class="ig-sub" style="margin-top:4px;">darker = more important for the predicted class</div>
      </div>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>
<style>
.cg-baseline { width:44px; height:44px; border:2px dashed #9e9e9e; border-radius:8px;
               display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center;
               font-size:16px; color:#757575; background:#fafafa; }
.cg-tok { border:1.5px solid #1976d2; border-radius:8px; background:#e3f2fd; padding:6px 10px;
          font-size:11px; font-weight:700; color:#0d47a1; white-space:nowrap; }

.cg-attr span { display:block; font-size:11px; font-weight:700; }

.ig-step { display:flex; align-items:flex-start; gap:14px; }
.ig-badge { flex-shrink:0; width:26px; height:26px; border-radius:50%; background:#0097a7; color:#fff;
            font-weight:700; font-size:12px; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; }
```

# Amazon & CLINC150: The Methodological Testbed

## Setup — A Testbed Before NAF {.center}

- Two public, **SOTA** benchmarks — chosen as a **testbed**, not the end goal. Most of the pipeline later applied to NAF (analysis, explainability, fidelity tests) was built and validated here first
- The only datasets where the **FATE (transformer)** architecture was tested — NAF stayed on the lighter FastText backbone

## Setup — Focus on Amazon {.center}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="34%"}
- On CLINC150, label attention doesn't just fail to help — it **degrades** accuracy vs. plain mean pooling
- Root cause: **too little data per class**. Label attention learns one attention query *per class* — 150 separate patterns to learn on CLINC vs. only 5 on Amazon
- ~100 examples/class on CLINC vs. ~40,000 on Amazon — not enough signal to learn 150 patterns
:::

::: {.column width="66%"}

## Training: What Shapes Validation Loss {.smaller}

960 runs on Amazon, swept across architecture, vocabulary size, and embedding dimension.

```{python}
#| label: load-amazon-runs-train

from pathlib import Path
import mlflow
import pandas as pd

CACHE_PATH = Path("results/amazon/runs.csv")
CACHE_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

if CACHE_PATH.exists():
    df = pd.read_csv(CACHE_PATH)
    if "metrics.train_time_s" in df.columns:
        df = df.rename(columns={"metrics.train_time_s": "train_time_s"})
else:
    df = mlflow.search_runs(experiment_names=["amazon"], max_results=2000)
    df = df[df["status"] == "FINISHED"].copy()
    df = df.rename(columns={
        "params.emb_dim":                  "emb_dim",
        "params.n_layers":                 "n_layers",
        "params.n_head":                   "n_head",
        "params.n_heads_label_attention":  "n_heads_label_attn",
        "params.vocab_size":               "vocab_size",
        "params.lr":                       "lr",
        "metrics.num_params":              "num_params",
        "metrics.test_accuracy":           "test_accuracy",
        "metrics.test_f1_macro":           "test_f1_macro",
        "metrics.train_time_s":            "train_time_s",
    })

    client = mlflow.MlflowClient()
    def get_min_val_loss(run_id):
        history = client.get_metric_history(run_id, "val_loss")
        return min(m.value for m in history) if history else None

    df["min_val_loss"] = df["run_id"].apply(get_min_val_loss)

    for col in ["emb_dim", "n_layers", "vocab_size"]:
        df[col] = df[col].astype(int)
    df["lr"] = df["lr"].astype(float)
    df["num_params"] = df["num_params"].astype(int)

    def arch_label(row):
        la = str(row["n_heads_label_attn"]) == "4"
        if row["n_layers"] == 0:
            return "FastText + Label Attention" if la else "FastText"
        suffix = " + Label Attention" if la else ""
        return f"FATE (L={row['n_layers']}){suffix}"

    df["architecture"] = df.apply(arch_label, axis=1)
    df.to_csv(CACHE_PATH, index=False)

COLORS = {
    "FastText":                          "#2196F3",
    "FastText + Label Attention":        "#00BCD4",
    "FATE (L=1)":                        "#FFC107",
    "FATE (L=1) + Label Attention":      "#FF8C00",
    "FATE (L=2)":                        "#CC0000",
    "FATE (L=2) + Label Attention":      "#880E4F",
    "FATE (L=4)":                        "#6A1B9A",
    "FATE (L=4) + Label Attention":      "#311B92",
}
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

### vs. Parameters

```{python}
#| label: fig-pareto-slide
#| fig-cap: "Validation loss vs. number of parameters"

import plotly.graph_objects as go

df_curves = (
    df.groupby(["architecture", "emb_dim", "vocab_size", "num_params"], as_index=False)
    ["min_val_loss"].min()
    .sort_values("num_params")
)

ft_archs   = ["FastText", "FastText + Label Attention"]
df_ft      = df[df["architecture"].isin(ft_archs)].groupby(
    ["architecture", "emb_dim", "vocab_size", "lr", "num_params"], as_index=False
)["min_val_loss"].min()
df_scatter = pd.concat([df_ft, df[~df["architecture"].isin(ft_archs)]], ignore_index=True)

fig = go.Figure()

for arch in COLORS:
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=[None], y=[None], mode="markers",
        name=arch, legendgroup=arch, showlegend=True,
        marker=dict(color=COLORS[arch], size=8, opacity=1.0),
    ))

for arch, group in df_scatter.groupby("architecture"):
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=group["num_params"], y=group["min_val_loss"],
        mode="markers", name=arch, legendgroup=arch, showlegend=False,
        marker=dict(color=COLORS.get(arch, "grey"), size=5, opacity=0.3),
        hovertemplate="params=%{x:,}<br>val_loss=%{y:.4f}<extra>" + arch + "</extra>",
    ))

for arch, group in df_curves.groupby("architecture"):
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=group["num_params"], y=group["min_val_loss"],
        mode="lines+markers", name=arch, legendgroup=arch, showlegend=False,
        line=dict(color=COLORS.get(arch, "grey"), width=2), marker=dict(size=5),
        hovertemplate="params=%{x:,}<br>best val_loss=%{y:.4f}<extra>" + arch + "</extra>",
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="Number of parameters", yaxis_title="Validation loss",
    legend_title="Architecture", height=460,
    xaxis=dict(tickformat=".2s"), margin=dict(l=50, r=10, t=10, b=40),
)
fig.show()
```

### vs. Vocabulary Size

```{python}
#| label: fig-vocab-slide
#| fig-cap: "Effect of vocabulary size on validation loss"

vocab_vals = sorted(df["vocab_size"].unique())
emb_vals   = sorted(df["emb_dim"].unique())

df_vocab_mean = (
    df.groupby(["architecture", "vocab_size"], as_index=False)["min_val_loss"].mean()
    .sort_values("vocab_size")
)
df_emb_mean = (
    df.groupby(["architecture", "emb_dim"], as_index=False)["min_val_loss"].mean()
    .sort_values("emb_dim")
)

vocab_offsets = {
    "FastText":                          -1050,
    "FastText + Label Attention":        -750,
    "FATE (L=1)":                        -450,
    "FATE (L=1) + Label Attention":      -150,
    "FATE (L=2)":                        +150,
    "FATE (L=2) + Label Attention":      +450,
    "FATE (L=4)":                        +750,
    "FATE (L=4) + Label Attention":      +1050,
}

fig = go.Figure()
for arch in COLORS:
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=[None], y=[None], mode="markers",
        name=arch, legendgroup=arch, showlegend=True,
        marker=dict(color=COLORS[arch], size=8, opacity=1.0),
    ))
for arch, group in df.groupby("architecture"):
    offset = vocab_offsets.get(arch, 0)
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=group["vocab_size"] + offset, y=group["min_val_loss"],

        customdata=group["vocab_size"],
    ))
for arch, group in df_vocab_mean.groupby("architecture"):
    offset = vocab_offsets.get(arch, 0)
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=group["vocab_size"] + offset, y=group["min_val_loss"],
        mode="lines+markers", name=arch, legendgroup=arch, showlegend=False,

        hovertemplate="vocab=%{customdata:,}<br>mean val_loss=%{y:.4f}<extra>" + arch + "</extra>",
        customdata=group["vocab_size"],
    ))
fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="Vocabulary size", yaxis_title="Validation loss",
    xaxis=dict(tickvals=vocab_vals, ticktext=[f"{v:,}" for v in vocab_vals]),

)
fig.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: load-predictions-slide

import numpy as np, urllib.request
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots

STAR_LABELS  = ["1★", "2★", "3★", "4★", "5★"]

PRED_BUCKET  = "https://minio.lab.sspcloud.fr/projet-text-classif/predictions/amazon"
ARCH_FILES   = {
    "FastText":                          "fasttext.npz",
    "FastText + Label Attention":        "fasttext_labatt.npz",
    "FATE (L=1)":                        "fateL1.npz",
    "FATE (L=1) + Label Attention":      "fateL1_labatt.npz",
    "FATE (L=2)":                        "fateL2.npz",
    "FATE (L=2) + Label Attention":      "fateL2_labatt.npz",
    "FATE (L=4)":                        "fateL4.npz",
    "FATE (L=4) + Label Attention":      "fateL4_labatt.npz",
}

PREDS_DIR = Path("results/amazon/preds")
PREDS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

preds_by_arch = {}
for arch, fname in ARCH_FILES.items():
    cache = PREDS_DIR / fname
    try:
        if not cache.exists():
            urllib.request.urlretrieve(f"{PRED_BUCKET}/{fname}", cache)
        d = np.load(cache, allow_pickle=True)
        preds_by_arch[arch] = {
            "y_test": d["y_test"].astype(int),
            "y_pred": d["y_pred"].astype(int),
        }
    except Exception:
        pass

ARCHS_AVAIL = list(preds_by_arch.keys())
```

### Error Analysis

```{python}
#| label: fig-error-seg-slide
#| fig-cap: "Prediction distance per architecture"

SEG_KEYS   = ["Correct", "Off by 1", "Off by 2", "Off by 3+"]
SEG_COLORS = {"Correct": "#43A047", "Off by 1": "#FDD835", "Off by 2": "#FB8C00", "Off by 3+": "#E53935"}

arch_segs = {}
for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL:
    d        = preds_by_arch[arch]
    y_t, y_p = d["y_test"], d["y_pred"]
    dist     = np.abs(y_p - y_t)
    n        = len(dist)
    arch_segs[arch] = {
        "Correct":   (dist == 0).sum() / n * 100,
        "Off by 1":  (dist == 1).sum() / n * 100,
        "Off by 2":  (dist == 2).sum() / n * 100,
        "Off by 3+": (dist >= 3).sum() / n * 100,
    }

fig1 = go.Figure()
for i, arch in enumerate(ARCHS_AVAIL):
    segs = arch_segs[arch]
    for seg in SEG_KEYS:
        pct = segs[seg]
        fig1.add_trace(go.Bar(
            x=[pct], y=[arch], orientation="h",
            name=seg, legendgroup=seg, showlegend=(i == 0),
            marker_color=SEG_COLORS[seg],
            text=f"{pct:.1f}%" if pct >= 4 else "",
            textposition="inside", insidetextanchor="middle",
            textfont=dict(size=11, color="white" if seg != "Off by 1" else "#333"),
            hovertemplate=f"<b>{seg}</b>: {pct:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
        ))

fig1.update_layout(
    barmode="relative",
    template="simple_white",
    xaxis=dict(range=[0, 100], ticksuffix="%", showgrid=False, title_text="% of test examples"),
    yaxis=dict(autorange="reversed"),
    legend=dict(orientation="h", x=0.5, xanchor="center", y=-0.22, yanchor="top",
                itemclick=False, itemdoubleclick=False),
    height=380, width=820, margin=dict(t=20, b=80),
)
fig1.show()
```

- The vast majority of predictions land within **±1 star** of the truth — off-by-3+ errors stay under **8%**
- Correctness rises modestly with capacity: ~59% for FastText vs. ~62–63% for the deeper FATE variants

### Model Agreement

```{python}
#| label: fig-agreement-correctness-slide
#| fig-cap: "Model agreement vs. correctness"

preds_matrix = np.array([preds_by_arch[a]["y_pred"] for a in ARCHS_AVAIL])
y_true       = preds_by_arch[ARCHS_AVAIL[0]]["y_test"]
n_test       = preds_matrix.shape[1]

n_distinct  = np.array([len(set(preds_matrix[:, i])) for i in range(n_test)])
maj_pred    = np.array([np.bincount(preds_matrix[:, i], minlength=5).argmax() for i in range(n_test)])
maj_correct = (maj_pred == y_true)

levels  = sorted(k for k in np.unique(n_distinct).tolist() if k < 5)
xlabels = [f"All {len(ARCHS_AVAIL)} agree" if k == 1 else f"{k} distinct labels" for k in levels]

share = [(n_distinct == k).mean() * 100 for k in levels]
acc   = [maj_correct[n_distinct == k].mean() * 100 for k in levels]

STAR_COLORS = ["#E53935", "#FB8C00", "#FDD835", "#7CB342", "#43A047"]
comp = np.zeros((len(levels), 5))
for li, k in enumerate(levels):
    counts = np.bincount(y_true[n_distinct == k], minlength=5)
    comp[li] = counts / counts.sum() * 100

fig = make_subplots(
    rows=1, cols=2,
    subplot_titles=["Share of test set & majority-vote accuracy", "Composition of true ratings"],
)
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    x=xlabels, y=share, name="% of test set", marker_color="#90A4AE",
    hovertemplate="%{x}<br>%{y:.1f}% of test set<extra></extra>",
), row=1, col=1)
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=xlabels, y=acc, name="Majority-vote accuracy", mode="lines+markers",
    marker=dict(size=10, color="#C62828"), line=dict(width=3, color="#C62828"),
    hovertemplate="%{x}<br>accuracy: %{y:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
), row=1, col=1)

for ci, star in enumerate(STAR_LABELS):
    fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
        x=xlabels, y=comp[:, ci], name=star, marker_color=STAR_COLORS[ci],
        hovertemplate=f"<b>{star}</b><br>%{{x}}: %{{y:.1f}}% of group<extra></extra>",
    ), row=1, col=2)

fig.update_yaxes(title_text="%", range=[0, 100], row=1, col=1)
fig.update_yaxes(title_text="% of group", range=[0, 100], row=1, col=2)
fig.update_xaxes(tickangle=-15)
fig.update_layout(
    barmode="stack", template="simple_white", height=380, width=820,
    legend=dict(orientation="h", x=0.5, xanchor="center", y=-0.32, yanchor="top"),
    margin=dict(t=60, b=110),
)
fig.show()
```

- Accuracy drops sharply as soon as models start to disagree
- Disagreement zones are dominated by **middle ratings (2★–4★)** — the boundary cases a human would also hesitate on

## Explainability: Self-Attention {.smaller}

*This slide only — CLINC150.* The one explainability angle not revisited for NAF, since NAF never used FATE's transformer layers.

```{python}
#| label: load-explain-artifacts-slide

import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path
from collections import defaultdict

import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots

EXPLAIN_BUCKET = "https://minio.lab.sspcloud.fr/projet-text-classif/explanations/clinc150"

_ARTIFACT_NAMES = ["captum.npz", "label_attn.npz", "class_vectors.npz", "self_attn.npz", "faithfulness.npz"]
_NOT_APPLICABLE = {("pooling", "label_attn.npz")}

def _load_artifact(method: str, name: str):
    if (method, name) in _NOT_APPLICABLE:
        return None
    cache_dir = Path("results/clinc150/explain") / method
    cache_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    cache = cache_dir / name
    try:
        if not cache.exists():
            urllib.request.urlretrieve(f"{EXPLAIN_BUCKET}/{method}/{name}", cache)
        return np.load(cache, allow_pickle=True)
    except Exception:
        return None

cap_la, lat_la, cv_la, sa_la, fai_la = (_load_artifact("labatt",  n) for n in _ARTIFACT_NAMES)
cap_pl, lat_pl, cv_pl, sa_pl, fai_pl = (_load_artifact("pooling", n) for n in _ARTIFACT_NAMES)

HAS_LA   = cap_la is not None
HAS_PL   = cap_pl is not None
HAS_BOTH = HAS_LA and HAS_PL

if HAS_LA:
    N_CLS = cap_la["word_attn"][0].shape[0]

    if "class_names" in cap_la.files:
        CLASS_NAMES = [str(c) for c in cap_la["class_names"]]
    else:
        import json as _json
        with open("assets/clinc150_labels.json") as _f:
            _lmap = _json.load(_f)
        CLASS_NAMES = [_lmap[str(i)] for i in range(N_CLS)]

    MODEL_LABELS = {"labatt": "Label Attention", "pooling": "Mean Pooling"}
    CAPTUM       = {"labatt": cap_la, "pooling": cap_pl}
    SELF_ATTN    = {"labatt": sa_la,  "pooling": sa_pl}
    MODEL_KEYS   = [k for k in ("labatt", "pooling") if CAPTUM[k] is not None]
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-explain-selfattn-slide
#| fig-cap: "Self-attention matrices per head and per layer, for a sampled CLINC150 utterance. One column per model. Use the ← / → arrows to switch between examples."

import json
from IPython.display import HTML, display

HAS_SA       = HAS_LA and all(SELF_ATTN.get(k) is not None for k in MODEL_KEYS)
HAS_PER_HEAD = HAS_SA and all("self_attn_per_head" in SELF_ATTN[k].files for k in MODEL_KEYS)

if not HAS_PER_HEAD:
    print("Per-head self-attention artifacts not yet available.")
else:
    HAS_TOKENS = "tokens" in SELF_ATTN[MODEL_KEYS[0]].files

    n_align  = min(len(SELF_ATTN[k]["texts"]) for k in MODEL_KEYS)
    lengths  = [SELF_ATTN[MODEL_KEYS[0]]["self_attn"][i].shape[-1] for i in range(n_align)]
    mid_idx  = np.array([i for i, L in enumerate(lengths) if 8 <= L <= 18])

    rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
    cand_idx: list = []

    if len(mid_idx) == 0:
        cand_idx = [int(np.argmax(lengths))]
    elif HAS_BOTH:
        y_true_ref = SELF_ATTN[MODEL_KEYS[0]]["y_true"].astype(int)[mid_idx]
        y_pred_a   = SELF_ATTN[MODEL_KEYS[0]]["y_pred"].astype(int)[mid_idx]
        y_pred_b   = SELF_ATTN[MODEL_KEYS[1]]["y_pred"].astype(int)[mid_idx]

        def _pick(mask, k):
            pool = mid_idx[mask].tolist()
            rng.shuffle(pool)
            added = 0
            for i in pool:
                if i in cand_idx:
                    continue
                cand_idx.append(int(i))
                added += 1
                if added >= k:
                    break

        _pick(y_pred_a != y_pred_b, 2)                                # disagree
        _pick((y_pred_a == y_pred_b) & (y_pred_a == y_true_ref), 2)   # both correct
        _pick((y_pred_a != y_true_ref) & (y_pred_b != y_true_ref), 2) # both wrong
        _pick((y_pred_b == y_true_ref) & (y_pred_a != y_true_ref), 1) # MODEL_KEYS[1] right, MODEL_KEYS[0] wrong
        _pick((y_pred_a == y_true_ref) & (y_pred_b != y_true_ref), 1) # MODEL_KEYS[0] right, MODEL_KEYS[1] wrong
        if not cand_idx:
            cand_idx = mid_idx[:8].tolist()
    else:
        cand_idx = mid_idx[:8].tolist()

    n_layers_ph = min(SELF_ATTN[k]["self_attn_per_head"][cand_idx[0]].shape[0] for k in MODEL_KEYS)
    n_heads_ph  = min(SELF_ATTN[k]["self_attn_per_head"][cand_idx[0]].shape[1] for k in MODEL_KEYS)
    n_models    = len(MODEL_KEYS)

    def _tokens_for(key, idx, L):
        if HAS_TOKENS:
            return list(SELF_ATTN[key]["tokens"][idx])[:L]
        raw = str(SELF_ATTN[key]["texts"][idx]).split()
        return (raw + [""] * L)[:L]

    def _title_for(idx):
        text   = str(SELF_ATTN[MODEL_KEYS[0]]["texts"][idx])
        y_true = int(SELF_ATTN[MODEL_KEYS[0]]["y_true"][idx])
        bits   = [f"true: <b>{CLASS_NAMES[y_true]}</b>"]
        for key in MODEL_KEYS:
            y_pred = int(SELF_ATTN[key]["y_pred"][idx])
            ok     = y_pred == y_true
            mark   = "✓" if ok else "✗"
            col    = "#2E7D32" if ok else "#B71C1C"
            bits.append(
                f"{MODEL_LABELS[key]} → "
                f"<span style='color:{col};font-weight:700;'>{CLASS_NAMES[y_pred]} {mark}</span>"
            )
        return f'Per-head self-attention — "{text}"<br>' + " · ".join(bits)

    def _layer_frame(idx, layer):
        per_head = {k: SELF_ATTN[k]["self_attn_per_head"][idx] for k in MODEL_KEYS}
        z_list, x_list, y_list = [], [], []
        for key in MODEL_KEYS:
            mat_layer = per_head[key][layer]
            L_k  = mat_layer.shape[-1]
            tok_k = _tokens_for(key, idx, L_k)
            for h in range(n_heads_ph):
                z_list.append(mat_layer[h])
                x_list.append(tok_k)
                y_list.append(tok_k)
        return z_list, x_list, y_list

    def _frame_for(idx):
        layers = []
        for layer in range(n_layers_ph):
            z_l, x_l, y_l = _layer_frame(idx, layer)
            layers.append({"z": [zz.tolist() for zz in z_l], "x": x_l, "y": y_l})
        return {"title": _title_for(idx), "layers": layers}

    frame0 = _frame_for(cand_idx[0])

    cell_px = 17
    tok_n   = len(frame0["layers"][0]["x"][0])
    plot_sz = tok_n * cell_px

    div_ids = [f"selfattn-fig-slide-l{layer + 1}" for layer in range(n_layers_ph)]
    fig_blocks_html = []
    for layer in range(n_layers_ph):
        fig_l = make_subplots(
            rows=n_models, cols=n_heads_ph,
            column_titles=[f"Head {h + 1}" for h in range(n_heads_ph)],
            row_titles=[f"<b>{MODEL_LABELS[k]}</b>" for k in MODEL_KEYS],
            horizontal_spacing=0.04, vertical_spacing=0.18,
        )
        z_l = frame0["layers"][layer]["z"]
        x_l = frame0["layers"][layer]["x"]
        y_l = frame0["layers"][layer]["y"]
        trace_i = 0
        for ri, key in enumerate(MODEL_KEYS):
            row    = ri + 1
            for h in range(n_heads_ph):
                col    = h + 1
                show_y = (col == 1)
                idx_sp = (row - 1) * n_heads_ph + col
                xref   = "x" if idx_sp == 1 else f"x{idx_sp}"
                fig_l.add_trace(go.Heatmap(
                    z=z_l[trace_i], x=x_l[trace_i], y=y_l[trace_i],
                    coloraxis="coloraxis",
                    hovertemplate="key=%{x}<br>query=%{y}<br>weight=%{z:.3f}"
                                  + f"<extra>{MODEL_LABELS[key]} L{layer + 1} H{h + 1}</extra>",
                ), row=row, col=col)
                trace_i += 1
                fig_l.update_xaxes(
                    tickangle=-90, tickfont=dict(size=9), dtick=1,
                    showticklabels=True, row=row, col=col,
                )
                fig_l.update_yaxes(
                    autorange="reversed", showticklabels=show_y, tickfont=dict(size=9), dtick=1,
                    scaleanchor=xref, scaleratio=1, row=row, col=col,
                )

        for ann in fig_l.layout.annotations:
            ann.font.size = 11

        fig_height = plot_sz * n_models + 155
        fig_l.update_layout(
            width=plot_sz * n_heads_ph + 180,
            height=fig_height,
            paper_bgcolor="white", plot_bgcolor="white",
            margin=dict(t=50, b=75, l=30, r=100),
            coloraxis=dict(colorscale="Viridis", cmin=0, colorbar=dict(title="weight", len=0.8, thickness=14)),
            showlegend=False,
        )

        x0_dom = fig_l.layout.xaxis.domain[0]
        last_xaxis = "xaxis" if n_heads_ph == 1 else f"xaxis{n_heads_ph}"
        x1_dom = fig_l.layout[last_xaxis].domain[1]
        y_bracket_bot = 1 + 20 / fig_height
        y_bracket_top = 1 + 25 / fig_height
        y_label       = 1 + 29 / fig_height
        fig_l.add_shape(
            type="path",
            path=f"M {x0_dom},{y_bracket_bot} L {x0_dom},{y_bracket_top} "
                 f"L {x1_dom},{y_bracket_top} L {x1_dom},{y_bracket_bot}",
            xref="paper", yref="paper", line=dict(color="#999", width=1),
        )
        fig_l.add_annotation(
            xref="paper", yref="paper",
            x=(x0_dom + x1_dom) / 2, y=y_label,
            text=f"<b>Layer {layer + 1}</b>", showarrow=False,
            font=dict(size=12), xanchor="center", yanchor="bottom",
        )

        fig_blocks_html.append(
            fig_l.to_html(full_html=False, include_plotlyjs=False, div_id=div_ids[layer])
        )

    frames = [_frame_for(idx) for idx in cand_idx]

    title_id = "sa-title-slide"
    blocks_html = "".join(
        f'<div style="margin-top:{18 if layer == 0 else 0}px;">{fig_blocks_html[layer]}</div>'
        for layer in range(n_layers_ph)
    )

    nav_html = f"""
<style>
  .sa-nav   {{ display:flex; align-items:center; gap:12px;
               justify-content:center; margin-bottom:8px; }}
  .sa-btn   {{ padding:6px 18px; background:#f0f0f0; border:1px solid #ccc;
               border-radius:5px; cursor:pointer; font-size:13px; }}
  .sa-btn:hover {{ background:#e0e0e0; }}
  .sa-count {{ font-size:12px; color:#999; }}
  .sa-title {{ text-align:center; font-size:13px; line-height:1.5; margin-bottom:6px; }}
  .sa-blocks {{ overflow-x:auto; }}
</style>
<div class="sa-nav">
  <button class="sa-btn" onclick="selfAttnNavSlide(-1)">← Prev</button>
  <span class="sa-count" id="sa-count-slide"></span>
  <button class="sa-btn" onclick="selfAttnNavSlide(1)">Next →</button>
</div>
<div class="sa-title" id="{title_id}">{frame0["title"]}</div>
<div class="sa-blocks">
{blocks_html}
</div>
<script>
(function() {{
  const FRAMES  = {json.dumps(frames)};
  const DIV_IDS = {json.dumps(div_ids)};
  let cur = 0;
  window.selfAttnNavSlide = function(d) {{
    cur = (cur + d + FRAMES.length) % FRAMES.length;
    const f = FRAMES[cur];
    document.getElementById("{title_id}").innerHTML = f.title;
    DIV_IDS.forEach(function(divId, layer) {{
      const gd = document.getElementById(divId);
      const l  = f.layers[layer];
      Plotly.update(gd, {{z: l.z, x: l.x, y: l.y}}, {{}});
    }});
    document.getElementById("sa-count-slide").textContent = (cur + 1) + " / " + FRAMES.length;
  }};
  document.getElementById("sa-count-slide").textContent = "1 / " + FRAMES.length;
}})();
</script>
"""
    display(HTML(nav_html))
```

- **~1.3M labeled examples** used for training

## Label Attention on NAF {.center}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="34%"}
- On CLINC150, label attention was starved of data — 150 query vectors, ~100 examples each
- NAF's usable training set: **1.2M examples** — by far the largest of the three
- As training size grows, label attention's validation loss falls **faster** than FastText's
:::

::: {.column width="66%"}
```{python}
#| label: fetch-mlflow-naf-slide

from pathlib import Path
import mlflow
import pandas as pd

RENAME_COLS = {
    "params.emb_dim":                  "emb_dim",
    "params.n_layers":                 "n_layers",
    "params.n_head":                   "n_head",
    "params.n_heads_label_attention":  "n_heads_label_attn",
    "params.vocab_size":               "vocab_size",
    "params.lr":                       "lr",
    "metrics.num_params":              "num_params",
    "metrics.test_accuracy":           "test_accuracy",
    "metrics.test_f1_macro":           "test_f1_macro",
    "metrics.train_time_s":            "train_time_s",
    "metrics.val_loss":                "min_val_loss",
}
KEY_COLS = ["n_layers", "emb_dim", "vocab_size", "n_head", "n_heads_label_attn", "lr"]

def arch_label_naf(row):
    la = str(row["n_heads_label_attn"]) == "4"
    if row["n_layers"] == 0:
        return "FastText + Label Attention" if la else "FastText"
    suffix = " + Label Attention" if la else ""
    return f"FATE (L={row['n_layers']}){suffix}"

def fetch_runs_naf(experiment_name: str, cache_path: Path, train_fraction: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    cache_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if cache_path.exists():
        return pd.read_csv(cache_path)
    raw = mlflow.search_runs(experiment_names=[experiment_name], max_results=5000)
    raw = raw[raw["status"] == "FINISHED"].copy()
    raw = raw[pd.to_numeric(raw["params.train_fraction"], errors="coerce") == train_fraction]
    raw = raw.rename(columns={k: v for k, v in RENAME_COLS.items() if k in raw.columns})
    for col in ["emb_dim", "n_layers", "vocab_size"]:
        raw[col] = pd.to_numeric(raw[col], errors="coerce").astype("Int64")
    raw["lr"]         = raw["lr"].astype(float)
    raw["num_params"] = pd.to_numeric(raw["num_params"], errors="coerce").astype("Int64")
    raw["architecture"] = raw.apply(arch_label_naf, axis=1)
    raw = raw.sort_values("min_val_loss").drop_duplicates(subset=KEY_COLS, keep="first")
    raw.to_csv(cache_path, index=False)
    return raw

df_frac13  = fetch_runs_naf("naf", Path("results/naf/runs_frac13.csv"),  train_fraction=0.13)
df_frac26  = fetch_runs_naf("naf", Path("results/naf/runs_frac26.csv"),  train_fraction=0.26)
df_frac52  = fetch_runs_naf("naf", Path("results/naf/runs_frac52.csv"),  train_fraction=0.52)
df_frac100 = fetch_runs_naf("naf", Path("results/naf/runs_frac100.csv"), train_fraction=1.0)
```

## Predictions: What Errors Look Like {.smaller}

```{python}
#| label: load-predictions-naf-slide

import json
import urllib.request
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path

PRED_BUCKET = "https://minio.lab.sspcloud.fr/projet-text-classif/predictions/naf"
ARCH_FILES  = {
    "FastText":                   "fasttext.npz",
    "FastText + Label Attention": "fasttext_labatt.npz",
}

PREDS_DIR = Path("results/naf/preds")
PREDS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

preds_by_arch = {}
for arch, fname in ARCH_FILES.items():
    cache = PREDS_DIR / fname
    try:
        if not cache.exists():
            urllib.request.urlretrieve(f"{PRED_BUCKET}/{fname}", cache)
        d = np.load(cache, allow_pickle=True)
        preds_by_arch[arch] = {
            "y_test": d["y_test"].astype(int),
            "y_pred": d["y_pred"].astype(int),
        }
    except Exception:
        pass

ARCHS_AVAIL = list(preds_by_arch.keys())

with open("assets/naf_labels.json") as f:
    NAF_LABEL_MAP = json.load(f)

with open("assets/naf2025_structure.json") as f:
    _naf_struct = json.load(f)

DIVISION_TO_SECTION = {
    div: s["id"] for s in _naf_struct["sections"] for div in s["divisions"]
}
SOUSCLASSE_LABEL = _naf_struct["sousclasses"]

def class_code(idx: int) -> str:
    return NAF_LABEL_MAP.get(str(idx), "?")

def code_section(code: str) -> str:
    return DIVISION_TO_SECTION.get(code[:2], "?")

def code_division(code: str) -> str:
    return code[:2]

def code_groupe(code: str) -> str:
    return code[:2] + "." + code[2:3]

def code_classe(code: str) -> str:
    return code[:2] + "." + code[2:4]

def code_label(code: str) -> str:
    dotted = code[:2] + "." + code[2:]
    return SOUSCLASSE_LABEL.get(dotted, code)
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Accuracy vs. Class Support

```{python}
#| label: fig-support-acc-naf-slide
#| fig-cap: "Per-sub-class accuracy vs. number of test examples for that sub-class (log x-axis)"

COLORS = {"FastText": "#2196F3", "FastText + Label Attention": "#00BCD4"}

fig = go.Figure()
for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL:
    d = preds_by_arch[arch]
    y_test_a, y_pred_a = d["y_test"], d["y_pred"]
    classes_present = np.unique(y_test_a)
    support = np.array([(y_test_a == c).sum() for c in classes_present])
    accuracy = np.array([
        (y_pred_a[y_test_a == c] == c).mean() for c in classes_present
    ])
    hover_codes = [class_code(c) for c in classes_present]
    hover_labels = [code_label(c) for c in hover_codes]
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=support, y=accuracy * 100, mode="markers", name=arch,
        marker=dict(color=COLORS.get(arch, "grey"), size=6, opacity=0.55,
                    line=dict(width=0.5, color="white")),
        customdata=np.stack([hover_codes, hover_labels], axis=1),
        hovertemplate="<b>%{customdata[0]} — %{customdata[1]}</b><br>"
                      "test support=%{x}<br>accuracy=%{y:.1f}%<extra>" + arch + "</extra>",
    ))

TICK_VALS = [1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000]
TICK_TEXT = ["1", "2", "5", "10", "20", "50", "100", "200", "500", "1k", "2k", "5k", "10k"]

fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="Test-set support for this sub-class (log scale)",
    yaxis_title="Accuracy on this sub-class (%)",
    xaxis=dict(type="log", tickvals=TICK_VALS, ticktext=TICK_TEXT),
    yaxis=dict(range=[-2, 102]),
    legend_title="Architecture", height=390, width=820,
)
fig.show()
```

- Below ~20 test examples, per-sub-class accuracy swings anywhere from **0% to 100%**
- Past a few hundred examples, it tightens firmly into an **80–100%** band

### Hierarchical Accuracy

```{python}
#| label: fig-hierarchy-errors-naf-slide
#| fig-cap: "Among wrong predictions, the coarsest NAF level at which they still land correctly"

import pandas as pd

LEVELS = [
    ("Section",   code_section),
    ("Division",  code_division),
    ("Group",     code_groupe),
    ("Class",     code_classe),
    ("Sub-class", lambda c: c),
]

ERROR_BUCKETS = ["Class", "Group", "Division", "Section", "No match"]
BUCKET_COLORS = {
    "Class":      "#66BB6A",
    "Group":      "#FFCA28",
    "Division":   "#FB8C00",
    "Section":    "#E53935",
    "No match":   "#7B0000",
}

def _finest_match(true_code: str, pred_code: str) -> str:
    for name, fn in reversed(LEVELS):
        if fn(true_code) == fn(pred_code):
            return name
    return "No match"

error_shares = {}
overall_acc = {}
for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL:
    d = preds_by_arch[arch]
    true_codes = [class_code(c) for c in d["y_test"]]
    pred_codes = [class_code(c) for c in d["y_pred"]]
    buckets = [_finest_match(t, p) for t, p in zip(true_codes, pred_codes)]
    overall_acc[arch] = (pd.Series(buckets) == "Sub-class").mean() * 100
    errors = [b for b in buckets if b != "Sub-class"]
    counts = pd.Series(errors).value_counts()
    error_shares[arch] = {b: counts.get(b, 0) / len(errors) * 100 for b in ERROR_BUCKETS}

x_labels = [
    f"{arch}<br><i>({100 - overall_acc[arch]:.1f}% of test set is wrong)</i>"
    for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL
]

fig = go.Figure()
for bucket in ERROR_BUCKETS:
    vals = [error_shares[arch][bucket] for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL]
    fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
        x=x_labels, y=vals, name=bucket,
        marker=dict(color=BUCKET_COLORS[bucket]),
        text=[f"{v:.1f}%" for v in vals],
        textposition="inside", insidetextfont=dict(color="white", size=11),
        hovertemplate="%{x}<br>" + bucket + ": %{y:.1f}% of errors<extra></extra>",
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    template="simple_white", barmode="stack",
    xaxis_title=None, yaxis_title="Share of wrong predictions (%)",
    yaxis=dict(range=[0, 100]),
    legend_title="Coarsest level where<br>the miss still lands right", height=390, width=820,
)
fig.show()
```

- Only **~7–8%** of wrong predictions still land in the right class
- The single largest bucket — **~47–48%** of errors — misses even the broad section ("No match")

### Hierarchical Accuracy — v2

```{python}
#| label: fig-hierarchy-cascade-naf-slide
#| fig-cap: "Accuracy by required hierarchy level"

cascade_err = {}
for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL:
    d = preds_by_arch[arch]
    true_codes = [class_code(c) for c in d["y_test"]]
    pred_codes = [class_code(c) for c in d["y_pred"]]
    cascade_err[arch] = [
        100 - np.mean([fn(t) == fn(p) for t, p in zip(true_codes, pred_codes)]) * 100
        for _, fn in LEVELS
    ]

SYMBOLS = {"FastText": "circle", "FastText + Label Attention": "diamond"}

fig = go.Figure()
for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL:
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=[lvl for lvl, _ in LEVELS], y=cascade_err[arch], mode="lines+markers", name=arch,
        line=dict(color=COLORS.get(arch, "grey"), width=2.5),
        marker=dict(size=10, symbol=SYMBOLS.get(arch, "circle")),
        hovertemplate="%{x}<br>error rate=%{y:.2f}%<extra>" + arch + "</extra>",
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    template="simple_white",
    xaxis_title="Required level of agreement", yaxis_title="Error rate (%)",
    legend_title="Architecture", height=390, width=820,
)
fig.show()
```

- Error rate climbs only gradually as the required match gets stricter — low at section level, rising toward sub-class
- The two architectures track each other closely at every level — essentially one shared curve, not two distinct ones

:::

## Explainability

- Trust and auditability in an institutional setting
- Detecting biases / systematic errors
  - <!-- TODO: example of M/K/J confusions, semantically coherent -->
- Assisting a coding officer rather than replacing them without recourse

## The Real Problem — and Where It Leads

> With a single predicted class, an error is an error.

The score doesn't distinguish "close" (right section, wrong subclass) from "completely off." So far: **one model**, predicting the sub-class directly — a 679-way classification in a single pass, no notion of section / division / group / class along the way.

- A fix: build hierarchy-awareness **into the model** itself, instead of just truncating one flat prediction after the fact
- Idea: **5 independent heads** (section / division / group / class / subclass), trained jointly on a shared representation
- Motivation: getting the fine detail wrong doesn't have to mean getting the big picture wrong too — **"smart mistakes"** instead of "wrong is wrong"

::: {.fragment}
**⇒ Towards Multi-Level Classification**
:::

# Towards Multi-Level Classification

## The principle

- 5 independent heads (section / division / group / class / subclass)
- instead of truncating the subclass code to infer the rest
- Hypothesis: getting the detail wrong doesn't mean getting the big picture wrong

## It works

- The independent section head is right **~61%** of the time when the subclass is wrong
- vs. **~52%** when truncating the wrong answer
- "Nothing correct" error rate: **~47% → ~34%**

::: {.fragment}
**That's what making smart mistakes looks like.**
:::

<!-- TODO: reuse a Python cell from the site here (pages/naf_multilevel.qmd,
     fig-hierarchy-errors-naf-multilevel or fig-hierarchy-independence-naf-multilevel)
     by copying its data loading + figure code -->

## A limitation: the loss isn't distributed fairly

- Each level weighs into the total loss in proportion to its number of classes
- Section: **~1%** of total weight — Subclass: **~40%**
- The section head — the most strategic one for a human who just wants to be "in the right ballpark" — is undertrained
- To the point of not beating simple truncation from the single-level model
